title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 169
paragraphs: When the Ionians had been thus ill-treated but were continuing still to hold their gatherings as before at the Panionion, Bias, a man of Priene, set forth to the Ionians, as I am informed, a most profitable counsel, by following which they might have become the most prosperous of all the Hellenes. He urged that the Ionians should set forth in one common expedition and sail to Sardinia, and after that found a single city for all the Ionians; and thus they would escape subjection and be prosperous, inhabiting the largest of all islands and being rulers over others. Whereas, if they remained in Ionia, he said, he did not see that freedom would any longer exist for them. This was the counsel given by Bias of Priene after the Ionians had been ruined. But a good counsel too was given before the ruin of Ionia by Thales, a man of Miletos, who was by descent of Phoenician race. He advised the Ionians to have one single seat of government, and that this should be at Teos (for Teos, he said, was in the center of Ionia), and that the other cities should be inhabited as before, but accounted just as if they were demes.
These men set forth to them counsels of the kind I have described:
